subject: Concurrency-to-throughput mapping + autoscale SLA review for private VPC deployment
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, daniel.park@acme-eng.com
Cc: partner-ops@edgecloud.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Concurrency-to-throughput mapping + autoscale SLA review for private VPC deployment

Hi all,

Attaching an initial concurrency->throughput mapping and a strawman SLA for autoscale behavior for the Acme private VPC deployment. Key asks:
- Can Acme confirm expected steady-state qps per customer endpoint and 99p latency target?
- Ops: what warm-pool sizing do we need to hit soft SLO under cold-start bursts?

Document attached: concurrency-mapping.xlsx (sheet: mapping + assumptions). I sketched three sizing tiers (dev/staging/prod) and a recommended autoscale cooldown window.

Quick notes:
- We assume 80% GPU utilization is the operational target for cost-efficiency.
- KV cache warms within ~30s for typical session profiles; prefix caching reduces per-request tokens by ~6-12% in piloting.

Next steps: please review the mapping and annotate the sheet with your numbers by EOD Wednesday. Daniel, if you can put your expected p95/p99 targets in the sheet that will help finalize the SLA wording.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Concurrency-to-throughput mapping + autoscale SLA review for private VPC deployment

Lauren —

Nice start. A couple of clarifying questions from my side:

1) The mapping assumes a static token length; can we add a small table that shows sensitivity to average token length (16/32/64)?
2) For the warm-pool numbers, what is the assumed model variant (fp16 vs quantized) — that changes per-GPU concurrency by ~20%.
3) Can we add a recommended ingress shaping rule (e.g., per-IP qps cap) we should include in the VPC ingress ACLs to protect the control-plane during big spikes?

I added comments on rows 12-18 in the sheet with suggested deltas. Linking a quick readout I used for similar customers: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1KmR2q-example

If no objections I can draft wording for the SLA paragraph about peak absorption (20-minute gradual scale to peak, immediate fallback to lower-cost regional variant if capacity not available).

— Jonas

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-eng.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concurrency-to-throughput mapping + autoscale SLA review for private VPC deployment

Thanks — small update from Acme ops:

- Expected steady-state: 120 qps aggregated across 3 endpoints (primary user-facing + 2 internal integrations). Bursts up to ~850 qps observed in our simulated load tests (short spikes, 3–5 minutes).
- Target latency: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms for the primary endpoint.
- Network constraints: egress capped at 6 Gbps from our VPC to Redwood peering. We are using a quantized LLM variant in prod (int8), so please size for that performance profile.

Two asks from Acme side:
1) We need a mutual action plan item that details how Redwood will scale across dedicated GPU pools vs. fallback model variants if we hit egress/CPU/GPU constraints.
2) Can you commit to a warm-pool minimum to guarantee p99 during 60s microbursts? If not, we need a documented operational fallback (e.g., degrade to non-blocking partial responses).

I put these numbers into the sheet and flagged the warm-pool row.

— Daniel Park
Senior SRE, Acme Engineering
acme-eng.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: daniel.park@acme-eng.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concurrency-to-throughput mapping + autoscale SLA review for private VPC deployment

Daniel — thanks for the numbers; very helpful. Based on the quantized model profile and the egress cap, initial sizing proposal below (high level):

- Steady-state (120 qps): 2 x A100-class GPUs with 8-way concurrency (conservative) giving headroom to 360 qps at 80% util.
- Burst cushion (850 qps peak): warm pool of 6 GPUs pre-warmed + autoscale ramp to 12 GPUs within 15 minutes. We plan to use a short-term token-bucket ingress shaping to smooth the 3–5 minute bursts and keep egress under 6 Gbps.
- Microbursts (<= 60s): guarantee p99 by holding a 2-GPU hot reserve dedicated to low-latency paths (this is the warm-pool minimum we can commit to initially).

Caveats and operational notes:
- If egress becomes the binding constraint we will fallback to a regional compressed-io variant that trades minor quality for ~30% lower egress. That will be documented as part of the mutual action plan.
- These numbers assume cache-hit patterns like your test traces (you flagged ~10% token reduction). If token lengths increase, we’ll revisit.

I attached an updated sheet with concrete concurrency-to-qps rows and a draft autoscale SLA paragraph (autoscale-sla-draft.pdf). Please review and mark acceptance points.

— Lauren

[attachment: autoscale-sla-draft.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, daniel.park@acme-eng.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concurrency-to-throughput mapping + autoscale SLA review for private VPC deployment

Looping in a couple of operational constraints we should bake into the SLA and runbook:

- Autoscale cooldown: 3 minutes scaling up (aggressive) with a 10-minute cool-down to downscale so we don't thrash on sustained oscillation.
- Cache warmup: empirical median warmup for your traffic is 22s; plan 30s for SLA safety.
- Admission controls: recommend per-tenant burst token bucket at 400 qps with progressive backpressure at 600 qps to avoid noisy-neighbor.
- Observability: require 30s metric granularity for GPU utilization and 10s head-of-line latency sampling for p99; we'll add traces to the routing decision logs.

I've updated the sheet with a proposed incident play (failover to compressed-io model + temporary rate-limit) and a short checklist for pre-cutover validation.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concurrency-to-throughput mapping + autoscale SLA review for private VPC deployment

Thanks everyone — action items and timeline: 

1) Acme (Daniel) to confirm final p95/p99 acceptance thresholds in the sheet by EOD Friday (2027-05-28).
2) Jonas to draft the SLA paragraph on peak absorption and fallback model variants (due 2027-05-31).
3) Marissa to convert the incident play and validation checklist into a CS-runbook (due 2027-06-03).
4) Ops (Lauren/Marissa) to produce a PoC run with 2x A100 + 6 warm GPUs in our staging rack (schedule tentative 2027-06-10).

We also flagged two risk items: possible egress bottleneck at Acme (6 Gbps) and the need to validate quantized inference latency at sustained concurrency >500 qps. If either triggers, the operational fallback will be: a) ingress shaping, b) degrade to compressed-io model, c) enable partial-response mode for long-tail queries.

Please confirm and I will push the timeline into the partner workstream and create a HubSpot task (HS-98421).

— Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Capacity & Optimization
Redwood Inference
